findings.title: Keep evicted device prompt caches owned until release succeeds

sources.symbol: Runner.storePromptCache 263-298; RestorePromptState 106-122
Generate prompt-cache insertion 269-286 passes ctx; decoded retention 304/406 uses WithoutCancel
deviceKVCache.Release 205; deviceCacheStorage.release 103; deviceCacheOwner.release 164
releasePromptCaches 430 returns failed entries; Runner.Close
Runner.SetLoRAScales 293-304 retains failed releases for retry
release 155 and close 165: checked-out allocations remain until returned or executor close

findings.evidence: storePromptCache first removes duplicate/over-capacity entries from r.promptCaches, then calls candidate.Device.Release(ctx) and clears candidate.Device even on error. deviceKVCache.Release returns context cancellation before releasing either owner. Therefore cancellation after successful prefill/upload but before eviction can leave the old allocation checked out with no prompt-cache owner able to retry. Generate's initial insertion and RestorePromptState supply cancellable contexts. Decoded-token retention already removes cancellation and is not the cited trigger. Existing releasePromptCaches and SetLoRAScales preserve failed releases instead.
findings.impact: A long-lived runner can retain unusable device allocations after interrupted cache replacement and encounter avoidable admission pressure. The executor pool still records allocations and closes them at shutdown; this is lost reuse/release during runner lifetime, not a proved permanent process leak. No runtime incident or leaked-byte measurement was obtained.
findings.recommended_change: Replace the duplicate eviction-release loop with the existing releasePromptCaches ownership contract, preserving the same-device exception. Keep any failed eviction reachable for retry, or complete cleanup under the established noncancelable cleanup context before dropping ownership. Preserve cache selection/capacity semantics and report errors honestly. An admission ctx check alone does not close cancellation between publication and release. Do not add another pool or cleanup framework.
findings.displaced_surface: Remove storePromptCache's unconditional Device=nil/ownership-discarding release loop in favor of the existing failed-release owner shared with SetLoRAScales. Retain exact token/LoRA/media identity, shared-device alias protection, cancellation atomicity and actual-completion release. No existing test deletion justified.
findings.comparison: Extend overgo/internal/inference.TestMultiplePromptCacheSelectionAndEviction with the canceled-context ownership fixture already used by TestDeviceCacheReleaseCancellationIsAtomic/TestDeviceCacheStorageReleaseCancellationIsAtomic. Verify error, old owner reachability, successful retry and no duplicate release, plus unchanged selection/eviction. Keep host/device generation continuation tests. Use native go test ./internal/inference -run '^(TestMultiplePromptCacheSelectionAndEviction|TestDeviceCacheReleaseCancellationIsAtomic|TestDeviceCacheStorageReleaseCancellationIsAtomic)$' when implemented; no new GPU workload is needed to expose the lost reference. SQA ran no reproduction.
findings.likely_effort: Small-to-medium ownership repair using the existing release result; handle aliasing and retry before considering a new field.

expected_benefit.outcome: Prevents avoidable retained device memory after canceled cache eviction and removes a conflicting cleanup implementation.
expected_benefit.uncertainty: Estimate production 0..+70/test +70..+160 AST nodes after replacing the loop, including alias/retry assertions. Correctness may require net growth; no claimed elapsed/byte saving. Existing fixture only; no schema, lane, framework or instrument added.

findings.plan_coverage: Both existing steps require prompt reuse and cancellation-to-release. Recommend this concrete ownership repair within that scope before longer-context reuse acceptance; no mandatory row or gate.
closure_criteria: Eviction cannot discard the last retryable cache owner on cancellation/release error; same-device replacement is not released; eventual retry/close releases once. Retained success, capacity and cancellation tests distinguish the repaired behavior from current source.

findings.evidence: Both projected-image generation and ordinary device generation execute the shared model but retain cache state through different owners. Projected cached layers materialize outputs and cache values as host reference.Value; the ordinary session binds retained device storage. Current expert misses still read encoded ranges and upload them, but staging is already reused and equal-sized victim reuse is fixed. Evidence a4da8aae393f6ae6ad59ef4d9cb6441febb57af59f79bca576138a45aea60805 preserves all 1065 prompt/71 output IDs: request 51.2466344 -> 37.6887321 s, prefill 27.5430087 -> 16.8896091 s, owned-device peak 38734030720 -> 38622966400 B, host working set 1863692288 -> 1789853696 B; release returns owned bytes to zero. No further performance change is proved.
findings.impact: Repeated state materialization and transfers remain credible costs in the active multimodal workload. About 19.4 s remains after prefill in language generation. Its exact split among state copies, expert loading, routing and arithmetic is not established.
findings.recommended_change: Use the existing retained cache/session and lifetime owners as the proposed shared boundary for ordinary and projected callers. Decide the smallest removal of host round trips with current matched evidence first. Do not merely remove the eligibility guard or enable graph capture across host routing. Do not add a second cache, CPU expert engine, permanent profiler or generic allocation pool based on this review.
findings.displaced_surface: If adopted, remove projected per-layer cache readback/re-upload and any replacement-only wrapper in the same change; keep one retained storage/lifetime owner. Keep necessary media-signature, multi-axis positions, recurrent/selection state, host-reference fallback and actual-completion release. No test deletion is currently justified.
findings.comparison: Lead deciding comparison: same screenshot/model/recipe/context and output work, existing ordinary versus projected execution owners, warm submit-to-complete and prefill/decode separated, exact media/output and cancellation/release, peak owned and physical device memory plus process working set/commitment. Reuse current baseline only with matching source/input identities. Retain TestProjectedPromptCacheRequiresExactMediaSignature and device recurrent/session tests; add only missing image-binding cases. Earlier retained-state evidence 31ff3f685bf7b2f4e392554732c8b4ba297d4f5d52c4160f8430324ca52407f5 raised device peak by about 429 MB and remains a rejection, not permission to repeat the same design.
findings.likely_effort: Medium; bounded comparison before implementation. A net reduction in state movement is required; code-size savings cannot yet be credibly estimated.

expected_benefit.outcome: Potentially fewer per-layer host/device copies and less duplicate state representation.
expected_benefit.uncertainty: Elapsed and memory gain unmeasured for the proposed change. Estimated production/test AST delta unresolved until a shared ownership design exists; fixtures/gates/schema additions should be zero. Necessary new numerical/lifetime coverage may add test nodes.

findings.plan_coverage: Existing rows cover the work and require matched performance/memory; no extra row recommended.
closure_criteria: Demonstrate net removed transfer/state work through the existing owner, or decline it using a matched comparison. Preserve output/media/position/recurrent semantics and cancellation release. Report complete code/test/setup costs and each memory metric; do not close final parity or 256K from a short screenshot.

device_newton_schulz_normalization.assessment: All owner refinements were applied before the deciding comparison. Supported Windows/CUDA execution required OVERGO_CUDA_TEST=1 and observed execution of both 8+2 FP32 and 4+2 TF32. The 514 scalar comparisons and 56 directions passed bitwise, including guard decisions, normalization multipliers, zero/tiny weights and thresholds around rounded FP32 squared norms. FP64 round-to-nearest scalar instructions were checked despite fast-math compiler options. Twelve alternating pairs across 32 cells compared preservation with reconstruction and counted bandwidth, launches and otherwise-skipped GEMMs. Normal cases ranged from no detectable gain to about 15% faster; every guarded cell was about 105-395% slower. The declared stopping rule rejected the candidate before further full-step/streamed runs. The unchanged production path remains. Optimizer-only gain could have qualified under the frozen 5% minimum, full-step regression and memory limits, but the guard-heavy limit failed. No candidate full-step improvement is claimed.
